newsitem.title: USA: Kurdish activist arrested for second time.
newsitem.headline: Kurdish activist arrested for second time.

text.p: A Kurdish activist, convicted in 1996 of passport fraud, was arrested for a second time on Friday and charged with grand theft, perjury and forgery for fraudulently obtaining more than $13,000 in federal and state college aid, authorities said.

Kani Xulam, who was born Namet Gundec but has used at least four aliases, was arrested by Metropolitan District Police and is expected to be extradited to Santa Barbara County, California, where the arrest warrant was issued, authorities said.

Xulam headed the American Kurdish Information Network (AKIN) in Washington, D.C. when he was arrested and charged with passport fraud in April 1996 after an investigation by the U.S. State Department's diplomatic security service.

Turkey and U.S. law enforcement authorities claimed he was the alleged leader of the Kurdish terror group known as the Kurdistan Worker's Party (PKK), which is fighting for independence or autonomy from Turkey and which the United States considers a terrorist organisation.
AKIN denied an association with the PKK and said it was a human rights group with a longtime committment to pacifism.

Xulam was convicted in that first case of obtaining and using a passport in the name of Steven Barry Citron, an 18-month-old boy who was killed with his family in a car crash in Louisiana in 1993. Xulam assumed his identity.
In that case Xulam was sentenced to three years probation and 400 hours of community service.

His arrest Friday was based on charges brought by Santa Barbara County, which alleged he obtained a total of $13,257 in student grants and loans provided by the federal and state governments when he attended Santa Barbara City College and the University of California at Santa Barbara.
Xulam used Citron's name to enroll in the university, obtain the loans, sign the checks and get a driver's license, according to the arrest warrant.
